Subject: Private GPU pool: sustained concurrency & egress budget review

Hi David,

Thanks for taking this on. We're mapping out the private deployment runbook for our VPC deployment and need to align on two things before procurement:

1) Sustained concurrency targets: our product team expects a steady-state of ~350 concurrent inference streams (avg request size ~1.2k tokens) with spikes up to ~1,500 for 2-3 minute windows.
2) Egress & networking: we have a hard egress budget (5 TB/month) for the pilot — we need recommendations for network shaping, MTU settings, and how Redwood suggests throttling/quilting bursts to stay within that cap.

I've attached our baseline load profile and a quick egress estimate. Can your team propose a sizing and a short list of ops constraints (warm pools, KV cache warm-up expectations, model fallback strategy) so we can approve on our end?

Proposed outcome: a 30-minute technical sync Friday (your timezone) + a one-page ops runbook we can include in the procurement RFP.

Thanks,
Jordan Li

Acme Corp

Jordan — thanks, received. High level notes before the sync:

- Sustained 350 concurrent streams at ~1.2k tokens is achievable on a small private pool if we (a) prioritize prefix KV caching and (b) accept model quantization to int8 for most requests. We'll propose a two-class SLA (gold/silver) so you have guaranteed low-latency for a fraction of traffic and a best-effort lane for the rest.
- For spikes to 1,500 QPS, the pattern matters: a 2–3 minute all-at-once spike needs either pre-warmed burst capacity or a graceful degradation plan (shorter responses / lower-parameter model variant).
- Egress cap at 5 TB/mo is tight; we should limit streaming chunk sizes and enable token-truncation defaults for the pilot. Also consider per-request compression for long outputs.

Can Naomi and Karthik lay out numeric sizing and network constraints? I'm happy to join the Friday sync as well. Proposed times: 10:00 or 15:30 PT.

-David
David Kim

Thanks — quick sizing sketch below (ballpark numbers for discussion):

- Baseline: 350 sustained streams, mean request length 1.2k tokens, mean response 600 tokens.
- Per-token CPU/GPU cost: assuming a 70B-class family quantized to int8 with Redwood runtime optimizations, expected ~5–7 tokens/sec per vGPU (varies by model).
- Suggested pilot pool: 8 x A100-ish vGPUs (or equivalent) with continuous batching and a warmed prefix cache for top 20% prompts. Expected sustained throughput: ~400 concurrent streams (meaningful concurrency is shaped by average latency and batching window).
- Spike handling: add 4 hot standby GPUs (burst pool) that can be routed to for 3-minute windows; autoscale with a cool-down of 10 minutes to avoid oscillation. For cost predictability, cap burst at 25% of normal RAM-backed pool for the pilot.

Egress/network notes:
- MTU: 9000 preferred within the VPC to reduce packet overhead for large responses.
- Inter-node bandwidth: recommend minimum 25 Gbps between GPU hosts for low-latency KV eviction and streaming.
- Throttling policy: per-tenant token-rate limiter + connection-level streaming limits; drop to text-only payloads when cumulative monthly egress > 80% of cap.

I've attached a quick egress estimate spreadsheet and a CSV of the load profile Jordan sent. Numbers assume a 50% compression ratio for output.

—Naomi

Couple of operational constraints from the networking side that will affect the final sizing and cost: 

- NAT egress: If the VPC uses a shared NAT gateway, egress metering will be coarse — recommend a dedicated NAT per environment so we can track pilot usage precisely.
- Load balancers: prefer L4 (TCP) routing for lower overhead; TLS termination can be at the edge if Acme requires SNI inspection.
- Packet loss and retransmit: tolerate up to 0.5% packet loss baseline; anything above suggests the need for flow-control via pacing at the application layer. That directly increases required GPU headroom.

Operational plays to stay within 5 TB cap:
- Prioritize compressed outputs and prefer summarized responses for long-form queries.
- Apply per-session sampling for diagnostic traces (only sample 1% of sessions to reduce egress).
- For spike windows, enable a circuit-breaker that routes excess traffic to a smaller, cached model variant (e.g., 7B quantized) with predefined degradation steps.

I'll add MTU and routing rules to the VPC diagram draft and share the PDF. Happy to walk through during the sync and pin down the exact numeric thresholds for throttles/fallbacks.

Irene Choi
Network Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
